title: Prove Yazelix Astra as a thin orchestrator
description:
Goal:
Prove the smallest useful Yazelix product assembled from accepted Orbit, Venus, Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig inputs while preserving one owner for each behavior.

Scope boundary:
This epic is planning-only until the user activates the Astra implementation frontier. Do not add runtime code, installers, CI, package manifests, compatibility layers, or duplicate child behavior while it remains deferred. Yazelix Nova remains independent.

Contracts:
AST-C1 through AST-C7.

Sequence:
1. Orbit proves the session and client-facing contracts Astra needs.
2. Venus proves useful native interaction against an exact accepted Orbit revision.
3. The user explicitly activates Astra.
4. Astra proves one Nix-only Linux composition and dogfoods it.
5. The user separately decides whether evidence supports direct-distribution graduation.
6. Accepted direct and macOS channels follow their own gates.

Success:
Astra stays a small policy, composition, diagnostics, and distribution owner. Exact child revisions and focused checks prove the product without creating a second terminal, renderer, editor, file manager, configuration system, or package graph.

title: Activate Astra after Orbit and Venus prove integration revisions
description:
Decision gate:
Do not begin Astra implementation until the user explicitly activates this bead.

Required evidence:
- Orbit names and proves the session, attachment, transport, and recovery contracts that Venus and Astra consume.
- Venus proves useful native interaction against an exact accepted Orbit revision.
- Both projects publish or produce relocatable artifacts for the selected target.
- No known P0 or P1 defect invalidates the boundary.
- The user chooses Astra as the active implementation frontier.

Acceptance:
Record exact Orbit and Venus revisions, proven contract IDs, verification commands, platforms, artifact locations and checksums, known limitations, and the user activation decision. Confirm that work on the previous frontier has reached its agreed handoff boundary.

Scope:
This bead approves a frontier. It does not implement Astra.

title: Define the canonical Astra component manifest
description:
Contracts:
AST-C2 and AST-C3.

Goal:
Define one small, human-reviewable manifest that pins exact child revisions, compatibility contracts, and declared package or artifact inputs. Nix consumes this graph during alpha. Later distribution tooling must extend the same graph instead of replacing it.

Reference and tool gate:
Inspect current child release and package metadata plus at least one comparable multi-component manifest. Compare a small hand-owned schema with using existing Nix metadata directly. Record versioning, validation, local LOC, maintenance, and the point at which external release tooling becomes useful. Defer cargo-dist, portable-bundle, and installer evaluation to the direct-distribution gate.

Acceptance:
- The alpha schema names project, revision, contract version, target, package or artifact input, and launch inputs.
- A focused validator rejects incompatible or incomplete component sets.
- One fixture pins accepted Orbit and Venus inputs plus Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig.
- Astra receives resolved component paths without constructing store paths or invoking a Nix evaluator during normal use.
- Product state records stable component identities instead of resolved store paths.
- docs/CONTRACTS.md records exact proof evidence.

Scope:
Do not require portable artifacts during Nix-only alpha. Do not create a second dependency graph for a package manager or rebuild child behavior in Astra.

title: Prove the smallest useful Nix-only Astra Linux composition
description:
Contracts:
AST-C1, AST-C3, and AST-C4.

Goal:
Prove one usable Linux vertical slice through one Nix-managed path. yzx launches an accepted Venus and Orbit pair, exposes Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig through their owned contracts, preserves one configuration path, and reports exact component versions.

Before code:
Review the accepted child contracts and exact proof revisions. State the process tree, configuration ownership, failure behavior, Nix composition boundary, and cheapest integration check. Run the crate and tool gate for every proposed runtime dependency.

Acceptance:
- One Nix flake path builds and installs the composed alpha in a clean Nix-enabled user environment.
- A user can launch, use, detach, reattach, and stop the composed session.
- yzx exposes a diagnostic version report tied to the component manifest.
- Normal runtime use invokes no Nix evaluator and product state persists no store path as component identity.
- Restart and partial-child-failure checks preserve declared user state.
- Astra contains policy and adapters only; ownership review finds no copied terminal, rendering, editor, file-manager, or Ratconfig state.
- Fresh-session dogfood records the exact artifact, commands, platform, and limitations.

Scope:
Keep the alpha Nix-only. Sidebars, popups, plugin surfaces, legacy compatibility, Home Manager, direct bundles, installers, and extra package channels require separate user decisions.

title: Design and prove the direct Linux release bundle
description:
Contract:
AST-C5.

Prerequisite:
Do not start this bead from completion of the Nix alpha alone. The user must activate distribution graduation through astra-db8.7 after sustained dogfood.

Goal:
Ship the proven Linux component set as a relocatable archive with an inspectable installation path that does not require Nix. Preserve the accepted Nix component graph and runtime semantics.

Reference and tool gate:
Compare dist, a small owned assembler, and other maintained tools that can consume the canonical manifest. Inspect archive reproducibility, checksums, signatures or attestations, installer generation, rollback, uninstall, multi-architecture support, dependency weight, and local LOC.

Acceptance:
- Publish an immutable archive, checksum, and signature or attestation for each accepted Linux target.
- Support manual extraction plus an installer with dry-run, versioned user prefix, atomic current link, upgrade, rollback, and removal.
- Preserve user data and avoid unrequested shell-profile edits.
- Verify on a clean user environment and record artifact size and closure contents.
- Direct and Nix installations report the same component graph and runtime semantics.
- Prepare yazelix.com installation copy without making the website the binary authority.

Scope:
AppImage, Flatpak, deb, rpm, containers, system repositories, and macOS stay outside this bead.

title: Prove Home Manager and direct-release parity with Nix Astra
description:
Contract:
AST-C6.

Goal:
Keep the proven Nix package as a supported channel after direct distribution and let Home Manager consume that same package and product contract.

Acceptance:
- The original Nix package, Home Manager integration, and direct release consume the same exact component revisions and compatibility metadata.
- Version diagnostics match across channels.
- Runtime behavior and configuration ownership remain channel-independent.
- A clean Nix profile and Home Manager evaluation pass without requiring the direct installer.
- Direct-install users need no Nix evaluator or store.

Scope:
Do not maintain a Home-Manager-only component graph, runtime contract, or feature. This bead does not expand the Nix-only alpha surface.

title: Design and prove native macOS Astra distribution
description:
Contract:
AST-C7.

Goal:
Distribute the accepted Astra component set through a native macOS boundary owned with Venus.

Reference and tool gate:
Review Apple signing and notarization requirements, Homebrew Cask, universal and architecture-specific artifact tradeoffs, application bundle layout, quarantine behavior, PTY and process assumptions, and candidate release tooling. Record cost, required credentials, platform support, local LOC, and exit conditions.

Acceptance:
- Produce a signed and notarized application or disk image for the selected architectures.
- Publish a Homebrew Cask over the same immutable artifacts and component manifest.
- Verify Gatekeeper, quarantine, first launch, upgrade, version diagnostics, and removal on a clean macOS user account.
- Record every Linux assumption that required a boundary or child fix.

Scope:
Do not simulate native distribution with a Linux-only package foundation.

title: Graduate Astra from Nix-only dogfood to direct distribution
description:
Decision gate:
Keep Astra Nix-only through alpha and early dogfood. Do not begin portable archive, installer, signing, Homebrew, or package-matrix implementation until the user explicitly activates direct distribution through this bead.

Contract:
AST-C5, informed by AST-C1 through AST-C4.

Required evidence:
- The Nix composition launches one accepted Orbit and Venus pair with Helix, Yazi, and Ratconfig through their owned contracts.
- Sustained fresh-session dogfood covers launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, restart, and child failure.
- Exact component revisions have no open P0 or P1 integration defect.
- Product code accepts explicit component paths, invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use, and persists stable component identity instead of store paths.
- The component manifest can describe the accepted product without using derivation identity as a runtime contract.
- The team has capacity to maintain artifacts, verification, upgrades, rollback, and removal.

Decision record:
Compare staying Nix-only longer with one direct Linux bundle. Name the user value, first target, release owner, expected CI and maintenance cost, tool-gate evidence, and features that remain deferred.

Acceptance:
The user explicitly approves distribution graduation and selects the first direct target. Record the exact dogfooded component manifest, evidence commands, known limitations, release-tool decision, artifact authority, verification plan, and rollback condition.

Scope:
This bead authorizes one direct-distribution slice. It does not implement the bundle or approve macOS, Homebrew, AppImage, Flatpak, deb, rpm, containers, or system repositories.
acceptance_criteria:
- The Nix-only Astra composition has sustained fresh-session dogfood evidence for launch, detach, reattach, configuration, diagnostics, upgrades, restart, and child failure.
- The accepted component set has no open P0 or P1 integration defect.
- Product code invokes no Nix evaluator during normal use and persists no store path as stable component identity.
- The component manifest describes the accepted product without derivation identity as a runtime contract.
- The tool gate compares staying Nix-only with one direct Linux bundle and records maintenance, CI, artifact-verification, rollback, and removal costs.
- The user explicitly approves distribution graduation and selects the first direct target.
- The decision records the exact component manifest, proof commands, known limitations, artifact authority, and rollback condition.
- Approval covers one direct-distribution slice and no additional package channel.
notes: Decision recorded 2026-08-04: Astra alpha and early dogfood use Nix only. Direct distribution remains a later adoption path behind this explicit gate. Runtime and product contracts stay distribution-neutral.
